"The humble appellant, therefore, prays that the Hon'ble High Court be pleased to :
(1) Admit the present appeal;

Further, the appellants alleged that the aforesaid land was taken over the possession by the respondent No. 2 and also handed over to the respondent No. 3 but they have not paid any compensation to the appellants and further the compensation amount had been paid to the other land owners.

The said prayers as sought for by the petitioners in the above referred writ petitions came to be dismissed by the Writ Court.

Challenging the said order dated 08.04.2011 of the writ court dated,
the intra-court appeal before this Court by raising grounds.

According to them, the respondent No.
2, on the request of respondent No. 3, has initiated a proceeding for acquisition of land for construction of new B.G. Railway lines from Jiribam to Tupul which falls within Tamenglong district by invoking the urgency clause u/s 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and in the year 2006 and thereafter, notice was issued under Section 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for acquiring the land to the extent of 84.233 hectares for the purpose of laying Railway lines between Railway Chainage 89.83 to 95.825 Kms. of Marangching (Makhuam) village from Jiribam to Tupul.

Subsequently, the District Collector has also submitted a proposal for payment of compensation for the land acquired in the aforesaid villagers and according to them, some land owners of the village also received compensation amount.

In the meantime, the respondent department has not proceeded to complete the entire land acquisition proceeding and not paid compensation to the land owners and said project has been uploaded and based on the new re-survey they are laying Railway line in the other lands.

Therefore, the appellant being the Chairman of the Makhuam Village has filed the instant writ petition before this Court for the interest of the aforesaid villagers for payment of compensation to the land owners.

7. According to learned counsel for the appellant, the appellant being the Chairman of the aforesaid villages, he has filed the writ appeal with a prayer to issue the necessary direction for declaring the corrigendum or otherwise under Section 6(1) of the Act, in respect of the final corrected chainage, to enable the 7|Page respondent No. 2 to take order for the acquisition of the land under Section 7 of the Act and to take up the fresh acquisition proceedings in respect of the final corrected chainage, strictly according to the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
According to them, the said prayer is maintainable.
Therefore, he has filed the writ petition before this Court.

The learned Single Judge,
without considering the case of the appellant in proper perspective, had dismissed the case on the ground that the respondent department, has not further proceeded, the land acquisition proceeding to acquire the land of the aforesaid village, for the purpose of laying Railway track B.G. Railway lines from Jiribam to Tupul and under such circumstances, when the acquisition process has been completed and payment of compensation also completed and they cannot question the modification of the aforesaid proceeding in the different place.
Therefore, they are not entitled for payment of the compensation and therefore, the prayer is unsustainable and hence, he seeks to set aside the order of the writ court.

8. Mr. RK Umakanta, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. W. Niranjit, learned Deputy Government Advocate, appearing for the State respondents has strongly objected by stating that Shri Meingamlung Gondaimei And Another vs The State Of Manipur And 7 Others on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155093707/
5

sentences.text: prayer sought for by the appellant/writ petitioner cannot be sustainable.

Subsequently, based on the new realignment, the aforesaid proceeding was dropped by the respondent department and the same is abandoned, and further states that though the land acquisition proceeding has been completed, the final award has not passed by the respondent.
Therefore, compensation amount was not paid to the land owners.
In such circumstances, the appellant does not have any legal right seeking for a Mandamus for directing the authorities to take over land and payment of the 8|Page compensation to the appellant.

In such circumstances, it is also strongly made an objection before this Court that the appellant has no locus standi to file the aforesaid writ petition for the land owners for payment of compensation to the aforesaid aggrieved persons.
The aggrieved persons have as not approached this Court seeking for any relief.

9. Considering the submissions made by the parties and having perused the materials available on record, the points of consideration for deciding the writ appeals are as follows :-
1) Whether the appellant is having locus standi to file the writ petition in the interest of the land owners?
2) Whether the prayer sought for by the petitioner for direction to compel the authorities to proceed land acquisition proceeding for the acquired land since the said project has been abated?
10.
This Court has fairly analyzed the submissions made by the parties.

The first point for consideration of the issue involved in the present writ appeal is that - Admittedly, the petitioner No. 1 as the Chairman of the Makhuam village, Tamenglong District;
Petitioner No. 2 is the village leader, the petitioner No. 3 is the Khullakpa, and Petitioner No. 4 is the Khunbu of the Makhuam village, of the aforesaid villages and it is not in dispute that the aforesaid land acquisition proceeding is against the other land owners' property and not the petitioners' property and the petitioner has filed the present writ petition before this Court on behalf of the other land owners which according to the law, they are not 9|Page entitled for filing the writ petition for the cause of the other land owners.
It is also clear that the land owners has not approached this Court seeking any other relief.
In this circumstances, the appellant has no locus standi to file the writ petition before this Court.

11. Secondly, the prayer sought for is for a direction to the official respondents to take over the said land of the villages which belongs to the said villagers and also pay compensation to the aforesaid villagers.

12. In the counter affidavit, it has been stated that pursuant to the notification for acquisition an award under Section 11 of the "Act" was issued on 28.11.2008 (Annexure A/1 to the writ petition)
and an amount of Rs. 2,19,52,270/- (Rupees two crores nineteen lakhs fifty two thousand five Shri Meingamlung Gondaimei And Another vs The State Of Manipur And 7 Others on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155093707/
6 hundred and seventy) was released as part payment of the compensation for the land and standing properties of the concerned owners and such amount were released to a group of allegedly authorized people including the writ petitioner Nos. 1 and 2.
13.

sentences.text: In the counter affidavit it has been stated that the alignment of the aforesaid railway line between Jiribam and Tupul was abandoned by the respondent department.
Neither the property was taken over the respondent department nor they have been vacated from the aforesaid land.
Therefore, in view of the decision taken by the authorities the re-alignment has been taken place and therefore, the respondent has not proceeded to take permanent physical position of the land.

In such circumstances, the appellant cannot compel the respondent to take over the said possession of the property though symbolic possession of the land was taken by the respondent department, but no actual possession of the property was taken over by the respondent department.
10
| P a g e

Further, it is also clarified that there is no documents produced before this Court that the said property was damaged by the authority and in such circumstances, part payment of compensation for the damages does not arise in so far as the aforesaid lands are concerned.
14.
Admittedly, the respondent has paid parts of the compensation amount to the appellant or land owners for the purpose of acquiring the said lands.
Subsequently, the Government has taken the stand for re-alignment of the aforesaid railway line between Jiribam and Tupul.
In view of the above, there is no merit in the appeal.

15. Mr. RK Umakanta, the learned senior Government Advocate appearing for the respondent department has specifically made the objection that the appellants are not the owners of the property since there is also complaint preferred for the payment of compensation, challenging the proceedings, WP(C) No. 603 of 2009 was filed and the same came to be dismissed with the observation that the appellant would be at liberty to submit show-cause statement to the impugned notice dated 5.10.2009 and the said order was challenged by preferring an appeal in WA No. 70 of 2009 and the same was dismissed.

Again, the notice dated 18th November, 2009 was issued to the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 and two others and the said notice was challenged before this Court in Civil Revision Petition No. 24 of 2009 but the same was dismissed by this Court on 30.11.2009 with liberty to submit appropriate reply to the impugned notice.
Thereafter, the petitioners filed a civil suit in O.S. No. 5 of 2010 before the Civil Court and the same is pending.
According to the respondents, the said fact was not disclosed.
11 | P a g e 16.
We have perused the order passed by the learned Single Judge.

The writ court has considered the contention of the appellant that there is no corrigendum issued by the respondent department but in the findings, the learned Single Judge has discussed that the Government issued Gazette Notification for realignment of the railway line between Jiribam to Tupul.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant was rejected.
Further, the learned Single Judge has observed in the order that the appellant cannot have legitimate or sustainable claim as owners of the land of the Makhuam Village.

The writ court also incorporated the contention of the private respondents by alleging as against the Shri Meingamlung Gondaimei And Another vs The State Of Manipur And 7 Others on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155093707/
7 appellant that they have concealed and suppressed the materials before this Court and filed the writ petition for the aforesaid prayer.

entities.text: Shri Meingamlung Gondaimei And Another vs The State Of Manipur And 7 Others on
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, we are of the view that the writ court has rightly discussed the contention of the appellant and the same was rightly rejected.
Hence, there is no warrant to interfere with the order passed by the writ court.

Further, we have gone through the relief sought for by the petitioner for issuing writ of Mandamus,
the same cannot be granted by this Court, without challenging the aforesaid Notification.
On this ground also, the contention of the appellants is liable to be rejected.

17. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants has also made a request before this Court that now the respondent herein has initiated the proceeding for recovery for the aforesaid part compensation amount paid to the appellants after a lapse of 15 years.
It is for the petitioners/appellants to work the remedy before the appropriate forum.
12 | P a g e 18.

Under this circumstances, this Court is of the view that the appellants have not made out the case to interfere with the order of the writ court and hence, the writ appeal is liable to be dismissed on the ground that the appellants are not the aggrieved persons.
Hence, the writ appeals stand dismissed.
